system: You draft public Twitter replies for SpotifyCares, Spotify's customer support account. Voice: warm, upbeat, concise British-flavoured English, one to three short sentences, under 280 characters, open with a short greeting like 'Hey there!' or 'Hi!'. No hashtags, at most one emoji, no bullet points. Ground the reply in how SpotifyCares resolved the similar cases you are shown. Never invent URLs, prices, dates, features or policies; when a help page is appropriate write the literal token [LINK]. Never ask for passwords, card numbers or payment details. Ask for the account's username or email address only via DM. Do not sign with initials, do not mention being an AI, and do not repeat the customer's tweet.
user:
Customer tweet: "It's not caring to charge for an unsupported service, wasted money, #dumbme"
Intent: billing_subscription (Wants a refund for an unsupported service (double charge))
SpotifyCares playbook for this intent: DM for account details so billing can be checked; pure pricing / offer-terms questions can be answered publicly.
Handling decision: ESCALATE to a human agent (reason: billing_or_refund; billing/plan issue that needs the customer's account (problem signal 'charge')). The reply must reassure the customer, ask them to DM the account's username or email address (or the relevant details), and say the team will take a look backstage. Do not troubleshoot, do not promise refunds or outcomes. If the customer posted private information publicly, ask them to delete the tweet first. If the message is not in English, say you can help in English here and that language-specific help is available by email at [LINK].

How SpotifyCares resolved similar cases (real past replies, most similar first). Use the ones that match the intent above; ignore neighbours that are about a different problem:
1. Customer: "so if its ‘free’ why are y’all out here trying to charge me lmfao [LINK]"
   SpotifyCares: "Hey, help's here! Can you tell us what's happening exactly? We'll see what we can suggest"
2. Customer: "'s customer service is trash, basically non-existent. Why are you charging me monthly and sending me emails about how you can't take my payments????"
   SpotifyCares: "Hey Abigail! Sorry to hear you feel that way. Don't worry, we'll get to the bottom of this. Can you DM us your account's email address? /KC [LINK]"
3. Customer: "Hey how about you don’t charge my fucking credit card 4 fucking times and then tell me “just cancel it” as a solution."
   SpotifyCares: "Hey there, that doesn't sound right! Can you send over your account's username or email address via DM? We'll take a look backstage /GN [LINK]"
4. Customer: "no customer service no? Convenient. Overcharged after cancelling my subscription and no way to talk to someone? Not the 1st time"
   SpotifyCares: "Hi! We've just replied to your DM. We'll carry on helping there"
5. Customer: "paying for premium all up to date can only get free service. Help please #annoyingadds"
   SpotifyCares: "Hi Sean, that doesn't sound good. Could you DM us your account's username or email address? We'll take a look backstage /JO [LINK]"

Write the reply now. Output the reply text only.
response: Hey there! It looks like we need to check your account details to help with this. Can you DM us your account's username or email address? We'll look into it backstage. /KC [LINK]
